quests.title: Possession of the Down Line
quests.blurb: Sunday night the line is mine until five. I want someone off the books to check something between here and Penrith, and I want it done before Monday, because on Monday it won't be there to check.

steps.label: two flat whites from the servo on Queen Street — nobody signs on without one, and one of them is his
photograph the eleven sleepers with the white paint on the ends, before anything happens to the white paint
clear the platform — the possession can't start while four blokes are on it arguing about whose taxi it is
ride the last down service before the buses take over for the weekend
photograph the whiteboard in the Penrith crew room, which already has next weekend written up on it
make $120 while it's still Sunday rates — after midnight it's ordinary time and you're worth less
Werrington, the fence at the up end: three letters go on it Friday and nobody has ever booked a cleaner
back to St Marys and show him what's on the phone

quests.title: Ten Fifty on the Ridge
quests.blurb: Eleven blue gums, a district view, and a garden shed that became a dwelling in April. Photograph them standing, before Monday. I can't be seen north of the boundary and my car is famous on that street.

steps.label: buy a flat white and carry it like you live there
get the train one stop; do not drive up there
photograph the eleven blue gums, standing, from the road
come back down the hill for where the shed is
photograph the shed they are calling a dwelling
settle with the six residents who come out filming
raise $200 for the consulting arborist's report

quests.title: Level Five, After the Last Train
quests.blurb: Top deck of the Hurstville car park. Starts when the last train goes, ends when the first one comes. One ramp, one boom gate, nine hundred windows above it. You're on load-in, security and the door. Column F.

steps.label: take the boom-gate key off Ada; her cousin wants it back by six
Penshurst, the lock-up garage, for the other half of the rig
the sub is a two-person carry and nobody in column F can park
two coffees at four — one for you, one for the bloke on the desk
run the door: fifteen on the ramp, cash, Ada counts the tin
the booze bus sets up on Forest Road at ten to four. Encourage it elsewhere
four come down from the towers in dressing gowns, filming. Be polite, be quick
photograph the empty deck at sunrise — proof nothing happened here

quests.title: Forty Groups Through the Door
quests.blurb: Nine opens between Blacktown and Rooty Hill and every one starts at ten past ten. Forty groups through the door, one lease. I've got nine clients who can't take the morning off. You can run and you don't scare easy.

steps.label: a flat white before the 6.40 key pickup
first open: the brick veneer off Blacktown station
photograph what the wide-angle lens cropped out
outlast ten tape-measure couples
run the western line out to Rooty Hill
second open: the duplex behind the RSL
take $200 in holding deposits nobody asked for
get the forms back to Lorraine before noon

quests.title: Nineteen Thousand Thirsty People
quests.blurb: Grand final at the park. Forty thousand go in, nineteen thousand never get near a bar, and every one of them walks past my gate to the station. Get them through it and the board can't sell my greens.

steps.label: eight meat trays out of Flemington, because that is where the trays have always come from
back one stop to Lidcombe and take the sprint in, standing, like everybody else
photograph the bar queue at the park: eleven deep, fourteen dollars, mid-strength
persuade eight of them that Concord West is a short walk and the schooners are seven fifty
the crew pegging a padel court over the number two green: ask them to stop, in the local dialect
two flat whites for Trevor, who has been rolling that green since four in the morning
two hundred over the bar and off the trays, cash, in the tin with the cricket club sticker
put the tin on the bar towel where Bev can see it
